model.rationale: The incumbent's overwhelming financial advantage, the district's Democratic lean, and market pricing near 94% all align behind Bishop, and nothing in the available evidence points the other way. overview:
Democratic incumbent Sanford Bishop enters the general election as a heavy favorite in this southwest Georgia district, which leans Democratic by about four points. Bishop's campaign raised over $1.1 million and reports roughly $448,000 on hand, while Republican Matt Day raised about $217,000 and shows no cash remaining, leaving the challenger little visible capacity to compete. No outside groups have reported spending on either side, and betting markets give Bishop roughly a 94% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, Bishop's incumbency, and the wide financial gap. Those fundamentals all point the same direction, and the race is rated Safe Democratic. The main uncertainty is the size of the winning margin rather than who wins.
